Maya (AE): Priya reports the POC stream is causing frontend JSON.parse errors mid-response. Happens intermittently on longer outputs.
Priya (Client): repro: open browser SSE to our POC endpoint, after a few events we get `Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected token \u0000 in JSON at position 0` and the UI crashes for that message. No 5xx from backend.
Liam (SE): can you capture the raw stream bytes with curl -N and show a hex dump? need to know if there are stray NULs or odd separators.
Priya (Client): pasted from curl -N | xxd: `... 7d 0a 0a 64 61 74 61 3a 20 7b 22 69 64 22xyz",22 64 65 6c 74 61 22 3a 22partial chunk\" 7d 00 0a 0a` — there's a 00 after the JSON.
Rafa (Oncall): 0x00 inside the stream will break parsers. Common culprits: proxy buffering inserting padding, backend write buffers with fixed block sizes, or a buggy upstream TLS terminator. Are you using nginx or a CDN?
Priya (Client): nginx reverse proxy + Cloudflare in front. We haven't changed write code recently.
Sam (Eng): on Redwood we've encountered proxies that pre-allocate buffers and pad with NULs when the app writes less than the block. For SSE you must ensure chunked transfer with exact bytes and no Content-Length.
Liam (SE): quick checks: 1) curl -N https://host/stream -v > out.bin 2) hexdump -C out.bin | sed -n '1,80p' 3) grep for `00` bytes near event separators.
Priya (Client): confirmed: hexdump shows `7d 0a 0a 64 61 ... 7d 00 0a 0a`.
Rafa (Oncall): nginx config suggestions: in the location handling SSE add: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_request_buffering off; gzip off; proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on; proxy_set_header Connection ''; proxy_read_timeout 3600;` Also ensure `sendfile off;` for the app if using some file send path.
Priya (Client): applied `proxy_buffering off` and `proxy_request_buffering off` and redeployed. curl -N shows the NUL bytes are gone on first pass; browser still saw one earlier today but much rarer.
Sam (Eng): there is also a timing class of issue where a partial event is emitted and the client tries to parse before the blank line delimiter arrives. Clients should accumulate until they see `\n\n`. Example Node pattern: `let buf=''; res.on('data',c=>{buf+=c; while(buf.indexOf('\n\n')>-1){const e=buf.slice(0,buf.indexOf('\n\n')); buf=buf.slice(buf.indexOf('\n\n')+2); const lines=e.split('\n').filter(l=>l.startsWith('data:')); const payload=lines.map(l=>l.replace(/^data:\s*/,'')).join('\n'); try{JSON.parse(payload)}catch(ex){console.warn('parse err',ex,payload)} } });`
Liam (SE): short-term client-side workaround: strip NULs before parsing: `safe = raw.replace(/\u0000/g,''); JSON.parse(safe)` — only until infra is fixed.
ops-bot: Deployed `poc/stream-proxy-fix` to staging (build #730) :white_check_mark:
Nora (Presales): is it OK to flip a tenant runtime flag to be stricter about SSE framing for this POC?
Sam (Eng): yes we can enable `strict_sse_boundary=true` for the tenant; low risk, will log any dropped padding. Nora please record in POC notes.
Priya (Client): after client buffering change + nginx tweak, we've had zero failures for 24hrs. thanks team.
Maya (AE): action items: 1) Sam/Rafa to draft infra doc with nginx + Cloudflare guidance for SSE routes, 2) Liam/Nora to add a short note to the POC report about the runtime flag and client workaround. Please add links when done.
Rafa (Oncall): logging follow-up: I'll scan edge proxies for other domains showing `00` padding and open tickets.
Sam (Eng): I'll create internal ticket to consider defaulting `strict_sse_boundary` for new POCs and include telemetry on padding occurrences.
Priya (Client): will include the final nginx snippet in our POC recap.
Maya (AE): thanks everyone  great pick-up and fast turnaround :smile:
